title: Strict-local base change model of a smooth morphism
statement: Let $f:V\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and let $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ and $\bar s=f\bar v$ be geometric points [def-weil-geometric-point] defined over the same algebraically closed field $\Omega$. Put $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$, $B=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{V,\bar v}$, as geometric strict local rings [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the canonical local map induced by `strictHenselizationMap`, equivalently by strict-henselization functoriality [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. Let $j:\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ be the structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] and $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ the canonical lift of $\bar s$ through the closed point. Set $W=V\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-fibre-product], $p:W\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\bar w=(\bar v,a)$, and let $w$ be its image. Then $p$ is smooth, $w$ lies over the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and the ordinary local structural map $A\to C=\mathcal O_{W,w}$ is flat and local [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Relative to the separable residue closure selected by $\bar w$ inside $\Omega$, there is a canonical isomorphism of local rings $B\simeq C^{\mathrm{sh}}$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] under which $\varphi$ is the composite $A\to C\to C^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and the residue evaluations into $\Omega$ agree. On spectra this isomorphism agrees, via the affine local-ring comparison, with the canonical strict-localization map $W_{(\bar w)}\to V_{(\bar v)}$ induced by projection; that map is an isomorphism over $V$. Both $A$ and $B$ are local rings and their maximal ideals are exactly the kernels of their canonical geometric-point evaluations into $\Omega$. If $S$ and $V$ are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], then $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The comparison and flatness of $A\to C$ do not require this extra Noetherian hypothesis.

proof.text: Use strict-henselization local structure for A and B. The codomain-restricted geometric evaluation is surjective onto its relative separable closure, so the evaluation into Omega is local; its kernel is the maximal ideal. Evaluate the pullback lift equation at the closed point to obtain p(w)=m_A. Functoriality supplies evaluation compatibility for strictMap, hence strictMap is local.

Choose an affine chart of S at the geometric image. The closed-point equation from functoriality and generization in a local spectrum factor Spec A through that chart. Apply the small-model affine-chart ind-etale theorem directly, avoiding the detour through the identity comparison. Base-change these local affine ind-etale charts by f, transport along pullback symmetry, and apply ind-etale strict-local invariance to q:W to V. Its isomorphism and the specified strictProjection satisfy the same structural and evaluation equations; functoriality uniqueness identifies them.

Smoothness is stable under base change, so p is smooth and flat. The canonical map from A to its stalk at p(w)=m_A is the inverse of stalkClosedPointIso and is therefore bijective, flat, and local. Compose it with the flat local stalk map of p to obtain ordinaryMap. No Noetherian hypothesis occurs.

Apply the actual-stalk presentation comparison to the geometric point of W, with the residue algebra fixed by descResidueField and the scalar tower through the ordinary residue field. It supplies H, P, and theta with their structural and evaluation equations. The ring equivalence opposite to the now-proved canonical strictProjection, followed by theta, is beta. Contravariance gives Spec beta = Spec theta followed by strictProjection; pointed functoriality gives beta evaluation compatibility.

Let d be A to C to H. Naturality of fromSpecStalk and the defining formula of ordinaryMap identify Spec d with Spec theta followed by the structural map of W and p. Precompose by the inverse of Spec beta to get a map from V_(v) to S_(fv). The pullback square and the strictProjection structural equation show it is over f. The theta and beta evaluation equations and the closed geometric lift show it is pointed. Uniqueness in strict-henselization functoriality makes it strictHenselizationMap f v. Cancel the beta isomorphism and use faithfulness of Spec to obtain beta composed with strictMap = d. This is a complete Lean calculation; no extra intermediate lemma is assumed for this compatibility.

For any locally Noetherian X and geometric point x, its ordinary stalk is Noetherian by the Mathlib stalk instance. Apply the actual-stalk presentation comparison at x. Its presentation gives IsStrictHenselization for H directly from the stored cocone. Strict-henselization Noetherianity makes H Noetherian; transport along theta inverse. Apply this general argument to S,fv and V,v.
